tier_error_bands.definition: Leave-one-out construction against the JANAF liquid Gibbs table, reported at Tfus and offsets +300/+800 K. Rows without a liquid reference point beyond the published table limit are omitted at that offset. Tier 1 uses each held-out row's measured values as an in-sample control; tiers 2 and 3 use leave-one-out estimates.
tier_error_bands.units: kJ mol^-1; dex per metal atom

alkali_m2o.source: Lamoreaux and Hildenbrand (1984), Table 1, p. 153, assessed K2O entropy of fusion, DOI 10.1063/1.555706.

fusion_temperature.source: Selected assessed melting temperature from the alkali-oxide trend and Gurvich/NASA liquid interval; the published constructions range from a silica-depressed lower bound to a higher assessed estimate.

ladder.source: 1013 K is the lower endpoint of the NASA Glenn CEA K2O(l) interval, based on Gurvich et al. (1982), TPIS Vol. IV, pt. 1, p. 377 and pt. 2, p. 406; the same value appears in the TKV database (Gurvich lineage, no further bibliography). The alkali M2O melting-point series supports this selection: Li2O 1711 K (Ortman and Larsen), Na2O 1405.2 K (NIST-JANAF/DTA), and Rb2O 778 K and Cs2O 763–768 K (Gurvich). Natola and Touzain (1970) report 919 ± 5 K in Pyrex, treated as a one-sided lower bound because silica contamination depresses melting.

alternative_assessments.source: Lamoreaux and Hildenbrand (1984), Table 1, p. 153; estimated melting temperature.
Natola and Touzain (1970), measured in a Pyrex container; treated as a one-sided lower bound because silica contamination depresses the melting point.

ladder.selection_reason: The alkali M2O melting-point series (Li2O 1711 K, Na2O 1405.2 K, Rb2O 778 K, Cs2O 763–768 K) places K2O near 950–1090 K. The NASA/Gurvich 1013 K liquid interval is consistent; the Lamoreaux–Hildenbrand 1190 ± 50 K estimate is high against the series, while the silica-depressed 919 ± 5 K measurement is a one-sided lower bound.

ladder.source: Lamoreaux and Hildenbrand (1984), Table 1, p. 153, assessed K2O melting temperature, 1190 ± 50 K. Retained as an alternative; the alkali M2O trend supports the selected 1013 K Gurvich/NASA interval.

fusion_entropy.source: Mean of alkali oxide members Na2O (33.95) and K2O (33.53). Na2O appears in the optimized Na2O-Al2O3 dataset, Table 1, p. 8; the K2O value is from Lamoreaux and Hildenbrand (1984), Table 1, p. 153.

ladder.source: No direct K2O fusion entropy measurement was available for this row.
Alkali M2O family mean: (33.95 + 33.53) / 2. Half-range spread: 0.21 J mol^-1 K^-1.

training_members.source: Measured Na2O fusion entropy in the optimized Na2O-Al2O3 dataset, Table 1, p. 8.
Lamoreaux and Hildenbrand (1984), assessed K2O entropy of fusion.

ladder.source: Leave-one-out Richards-type estimate from the declared 48-pair census: mean fusion entropy per formula atom across the 47 other compounds, including oxygen, multiplied by K2O’s 3 atoms. The rule is known to fail badly.

training_provenance.normalization: mean of fusion_entropy / total_atoms, multiplied by the target formula atom count

liquid_heat_capacity.source: Arithmetic mean of K2O partial-molar values 97.0 ± 5.1 and 98.5 ± 5.5 J mol^-1 K^-1; the larger reported spread is retained.

ladder.source: No direct K2O liquid heat-capacity measurement was available for this row.

fusion_temperature_fallback.name: extrapolated liquidus
fusion_temperature_fallback.method: For an incongruently melting or decomposing solid, use a cited hypothetical fusion temperature. Record each cited construction and use their minimum and maximum as the temperature band; propagate the endpoints through the crystal interpolation and liquid construction.
